title: Records with Morton and being denied solo records
summary: He made a couple of records with Morton, kept up novelty work, and Ink Williams never had enough wax for his solo piano and vocal numbers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, a piece of paper on it.

And I forget his name now at that time. And anyhow, he says to me, he says, well, gee whiz, you sound almost like that cone yet, and still you got a little more power behind it. And he says, I'm going to get you to make a couple of records with me. And Jell-O'-Roll got me to make a couple of records with him and the guy on the cone and me on his own horn. And so I kept it going for a novelty use for a number of years, and so back and forth with Jimmy O'Brien, Jimmy Blythe. And so I kept on recording around that way until after years passed in between with Mayo, which we always called him Ink Williams. And so I used to try to get Ink to let me do a number by myself on piano and sing. But he always didn't have enough wax.
He was running short of wax, this, that, and the other.
